introduction: This foundational level establishes the fundamental relationships between heat, work, and internal energy. It introduces the Zeroth and First Laws of Thermodynamics, alongside the macroscopic and microscopic behavior of ideal gases.

core_concepts.title: Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics
core_concepts.description: The concept of Thermal Equilibrium: If systems A and B are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system C, then A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other ($T_A = T_B, T_B = T_C \Rightarrow T_A = T_C$). This law fundamentally defines Temperature.

core_concepts.title: First Law of Thermodynamics
core_concepts.description: An application of the Conservation of Energy. The heat supplied to a system ($Q$) is equal to the sum of the increase in its internal energy ($\Delta U$) and the work done by the system ($W$): $Q = \Delta U + W$.

core_concepts.title: Ideal Gas Equation
core_concepts.description: The equation of state connecting macroscopic variables: $PV = nRT$ (where $P$ is pressure, $V$ is volume, $n$ is number of moles, $R$ is the universal gas constant, and $T$ is absolute temperature).

core_concepts.title: Assumptions of KTG
core_concepts.description: Gas molecules are considered point masses, all collisions (between molecules and with walls) are perfectly elastic, and there are completely no intermolecular forces of attraction or repulsion.

important_entities.name: Internal Energy ($U$)
important_entities.key_fact: For an ideal gas, $U$ is strictly a function of Temperature ($T$) only.
important_entities.significance: Since it is a state function, if the initial and final temperatures are the same (like in an isothermal or cyclic process), the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta U = 0$).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In Physics, work done BY the gas (expansion) is taken as positive ($+W$), and work done ON the gas (compression) is negative ($-W$). Be highly careful, as this is often the exact opposite of the convention used in Chemistry.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Back to start = Zero Internal Change
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In any cyclic process, the system returns to its initial state, meaning $\Delta U = 0$. Therefore, by the First Law, the total heat added equals the total work done ($Q = W$).

exam_strategy_tips: The area strictly under the P-V graph (Indicator Diagram) represents the Work Done ($W$). If a thermodynamic cycle on a P-V graph is clockwise, the net work is positive; if anticlockwise, it is negative.
